XMLBIF 0.3 — Experimental and educational authoring profile, revision 2 (2026-10-04)
PURPOSE AND USE This file is an XML Schema 1.0 validator, despite its requested .xml suffix. It validates XMLBIF structure for experimental and educational networks. One NETWORK per question is recommended; multiple NETWORK elements may share a BIF document. This schema supplies no networks or probabilities. Instance elements have no namespace. Validate explicitly, for example: xmllint --nonet --noout --schema schema.xml model.xmlbif Alternatively set xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" and xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="schema.xml" on the instance's BIF element. The validator must actually load this schema; a schema-location hint alone does not perform validation. Disable external entities and network fetching.
PROFILE BOUNDARY Based on raw/md/The Interchange Format for Bayesian Networks.md, sections "The XMLBIF format" and "Outside XML", and the corresponding wiki source note. Online specification checked 2026-09-16: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs/user/fgcozman/www/Research/InterchangeFormat/ This is a deliberately stricter authoring subset, not an exact DTD translation: * VERSION is exactly 0.3 and at least one NETWORK is required. * Identifiers follow the written ASCII rule [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*. The original Dog-Problem example contradicts that rule by using hyphens; those identifiers need consistent renaming to validate against this profile. * Each DEFINITION has exactly one FOR and one nonempty TABLE. The original permits repeated TABLE elements with last-table-wins semantics; this profile rejects them to avoid silent replacement of experimental parameters. * Tables contain finite IEEE-754 double values in decimal/scientific notation. Negative utility values are allowed; NaN, infinities and overflow are not. * Network names are unique per document; variable names and definition targets are unique per network; outcomes are unique per variable; GIVEN names are unique per definition. FOR and GIVEN must name a variable in the same network. NETWORK children after NAME, VARIABLE children after NAME, and DEFINITION children may be interleaved. GIVEN and OUTCOME order remain semantically significant. PROPERTY remains arbitrary Unicode text, with no custom tags.
BACKGROUND SOURCES AND EXPERIMENTAL MODELING medical-knowledge/02-md/guideline-statement-summary.md, sections Assessment and Determination of Treatment Plan, Pharmacotherapy, and Psychosocial Interventions, distinguishes 24 statements. Standalone STATEMENT-01.md through STATEMENT-14.md cover assessment, quantitative measurement, treatment planning, antipsychotic selection/continuation, clozapine, LAIs, and movement adverse effects. Appendix-C.md includes evidence sections for statements 1 through 24; Appendix-D.md has intervention-specific strength-of-evidence tables. Glossary, acronyms, development process and appendices are supporting sources, not each a separate question. These sources provide optional background attribution; their electronic-decision-support restrictions do not gate experiments in this educational application. The schema does not enumerate a fixed set of network names, drugs, diagnoses, scales, states or treatment thresholds.
Scenario inputs may be synthetic, manually supplied or simulated. Supporting clinical records, instruments, dated assessments and clinician verification are optional, rather than input prerequisites. Observations are optional; a parameterized model may infer with a subset of observations or none.
Priors and CPTs may be supplied manually, generated for a synthetic example or estimated by an LLM, then adjusted for the experiment. Fixed clinician-review mappings are not required. Output names describe experimental topics; their conditional distributions are supplied per run. Ordered proposed_parent properties preserve draft edges until a DEFINITION with corresponding ordered GIVEN elements and a complete TABLE is supplied. Generic XMLBIF importers do not interpret proposed_parent properties as edges.
Nature, decision and utility variables are all supported. An observed treatment is a nature variable; a controllable action in an influence diagram is decision. A posterior probability of an action is distinct from an expected-utility recommendation. Optional recommendation-strength and evidence-quality metadata are source annotations, not probability values. Historical source-category lookups are examples of ordinal drug attributes, not patient event probabilities.
OPTIONAL PROPERTY CONVENTION (DESIGN PROPOSAL, NOT XSD-ENFORCED) Use one key=value entry per PROPERTY; repeat source entries when needed. Network: clinical_question, use_context, input_policy, parameter_policy, inference_mode, graph_semantics, edge_encoding, execution_contract, source_policy, source_path, source_locator, source_sha256, source_version, statement_id, recommendation_strength, evidence_quality, population, setting, time_horizon, model_version, validation_status. Variable: label, clinical_role, definition, terminology_system, terminology_code, instrument, units, time_window, discretization, missingness_policy, proposed_parent, parameter_status, required_table_entries, source_path, source_locator. Definition: parameter_method, parameter_status, source_path, source_locator, population, time_horizon, elicitation_date, reviewer, uncertainty_description. For example: source_path=medical-knowledge/02-md/STATEMENT-07.md and source_locator=Identification of Treatment-Resistant Schizophrenia. parameter_method may describe manual, synthetic, llm_estimated, source_reported or elicited values. Source and reviewer fields are optional. Source annotations remain separate from experiment-specific assumptions and estimates. These keys are advisory. PROPERTY syntax, presence, clinical meaning, and source freshness are not checked here. Doses and monitoring schedules from the historical guideline are not embedded as current prescribing rules.
CHECKS REQUIRED OUTSIDE THIS XSD BEFORE INFERENCE 1. At least one variable per network; an acyclic graph without self-parenting. No cross-network edges; combine networks explicitly if dependencies exist. 2. Nature and decision variables need a nonempty, mutually exclusive and exhaustive outcome set. Utility variables use scalar utility tables, not categorical probability distributions; check engine-specific conventions. 3. Every nature variable needs a definition (including root priors). Decision nodes may omit a probability table; informational parents/policies and utility definitions need engine-specific influence-diagram validation. 4. For nature X with ordered parents P1,...,Pk, TABLE length must equal |X| times the product of |Pi|. X changes fastest, Pk next, P1 slowest, following declaration order. Each conditional row must lie in [0,1] and sum to 1 within a documented tolerance. Utility tables have one real value per parent configuration and are not normalized as probabilities. 5. Draft networks may omit CPTs during authoring. Before execution, supply complete tables, including root priors, using the experiment's chosen parameter method. Synthetic or uniform examples are allowed. A named but empty NETWORK or an undefined nature variable can pass this format validator; neither is a complete executable model. 6. An unspecified scenario input means no observation is entered. A complete model can infer without observing every input. Scenario observations are supplied separately; XMLBIF 0.3 has no standard observation element.
